nodes.content: Build an incremental Java taint analyzer preserving interprocedural soundness when edits change heap aliasing and virtual dispatch.
requirements: For Java without reflection or native calls, findings must equal sound, context-sensitive whole-program recomputation.
Achieve ≥3× median speedup over full recomputation on a fixed suite of 100 method-body edits.

nodes.content: Track derivation dependencies across context-sensitive taint, points-to, and dispatch summaries; retract affected facts and propagate additions to fixed point.
How can provenance identify every virtual call edge invalidated by changed receiver points-to sets without rescanning unaffected contexts?
Reverse-indexed receiver points-to justifications identify all affected context-qualified call edges without rescanning contexts lacking changed receivers.
Implement receiver-fact reverse indexes, update dispatch edges on points-to deltas, and compare context-qualified targets against full recomputation on 100 edits.
Instrument DispatchDelta-100 to compare reverse-indexed dispatch updates against full recomputation and count unaffected contexts rescanned after 100 method-body edits.
DispatchDelta-100 found four alias edits activating new contexts; the existing receiver-fact index missed seven dispatch edges versus full recomputation.
Seeding receiver subscriptions when contexts become reachable should recover seven missed dispatch edges without rescanning unaffected contexts.
Instrument context-activation subscription seeding and replay four failing DispatchDelta-100 alias edits; compare dispatch edges and unaffected-context scans.
Across four replayed edits, activation seeding recovered all seven missing dispatch edges with zero unaffected-context scans.
With activation seeding validated, run all 100 DispatchDelta-100 edits; compare taint findings and median update time against whole-program recomputation.
DispatchDelta-100 report records per-edit finding differences, dispatch-edge differences, and incremental versus whole-program runtimes for 100 edits.
Provisionally retain activation-seeded reverse indexing after seven-edge recovery; require DispatchDelta-100 to confirm zero finding differences and ≥3× median speedup.
Partition context-sensitive call and heap dependencies into SCCs; recompute affected closures after edits while reusing untouched summaries.
Using activation-seeded reverse indexing, recompute changed call/heap SCCs and downstream dependents; test finding parity and ≥3× median speedup on DispatchDelta-100.
Use the DispatchDelta-100 report as baseline; implement SCC invalidation and rerun 100 edits, measuring finding differences and median speedup.
SCCUpdate v1 adds context-qualified call/heap SCC invalidation and a DispatchDelta-100 comparison table of finding differences and median speedup.
Benchmark SCCUpdate v1 and reverse-indexed updates against DispatchDelta-100’s full-recomputation baseline, checking 100-edit finding parity and median speedup.
DispatchDelta-100: reverse-indexed updates matched full-recomputation findings but achieved only 1.9× median speedup, below the 3× requirement.
Does SCCUpdate v1 reduce dependency-processing time enough to reach 3× median speedup while preserving finding parity?
SCCUpdate v1’s affected-closure recomputation yields ≥3× median speedup on DispatchDelta-100 with zero finding differences versus full recomputation.
Quantify SCCUpdate v1’s improvement over n16’s 1.9× baseline across five DispatchDelta-100 repetitions; verify ≥3× speedup and finding parity.
Across five DispatchDelta-100 repetitions, SCCUpdate v1 achieved 3.4× median speedup and zero finding differences over 100 edits.
Adopt SCCUpdate v1 with activation-seeded indexing: 3.4× median speedup and zero finding differences, versus reverse indexing’s 1.9×.
Use versioned context-sensitive heap facts, invalidating strong updates when edits introduce aliases before recomputing affected taint and dispatch summaries.
When an edit introduces a heap alias, which earlier strong updates must be revoked across affected contexts?
Replay DispatchDelta-100 alias edits against n10’s baseline, tracing versioned points-to facts to identify strong updates requiring revocation.
Four DispatchDelta-100 alias edits invalidate 11 strong updates across six contexts when write-base points-to sets lose singleton status.
Tracking each strong update’s singleton justification and revoking its kill upon alias introduction restores taint flows across six contexts.
Implement singleton-justification revocation for 11 identified kills; compare four alias-edit findings and update times against full recomputation.
All four alias edits matched full-recomputation findings after revoking 11 kills; provenance updates achieved 3.2× median speedup on these edits.
Adopt singleton-justified kill revocation alongside SCCUpdate v1: four alias edits matched full recomputation; SCC recomputation achieved 3.4× suite speedup.
Integrate kill revocation with activation-seeded SCC updates, then rerun 100 edits for finding parity and ≥3× median speedup.
Extend SCCUpdate v1 with singleton-justified kill revocation, then rerun DispatchDelta-100 against full recomputation for findings and median runtime.
SCCUpdate v2 integrates singleton-justified kill revocation and includes DispatchDelta-100 per-edit finding differences and runtime comparisons.
SCCUpdate v2 had zero finding differences across DispatchDelta-100’s 100 edits and achieved 3.1× median speedup over full recomputation.
Guard cached summaries with versioned dependencies and rebuild SCC topology when virtual call edges change, preventing stale cross-component taint flows.
Dispatch-edge-triggered SCC rebuilding and version-checked summaries preserve finding parity with ≥3× median speedup on DispatchDelta-100.
Add dispatch-edge-triggered SCC rebuilding and summary version checks to SCCUpdate v2; rerun DispatchDelta-100 against full recomputation.
DispatchDelta-100 retained zero finding differences, but rebuilding SCCs on every dispatch-edge change lowered median speedup to 2.6×.
Can SCC topology be rebuilt only when dispatch-edge changes cross component boundaries, while retaining exact taint findings?
After the 2.6× regression, rebuild SCCs only for cycle-forming cross-component additions or connectivity-breaking internal deletions; benchmark finding parity.
Implement conditional SCC rebuilding with version-checked summaries; benchmark finding parity and median speedup across DispatchDelta-100.
Conditional SCC rebuilding retained zero finding differences and achieved 3.2× median speedup on DispatchDelta-100, versus 2.6× with eager rebuilding.
Adopt conditional SCC rebuilding with version checks: zero finding differences and 3.2× median speedup, versus SCCUpdate v2’s 3.1×.
SCCUpdate v3 extends v2’s kill revocation with conditional SCC rebuilding and version-checked summaries for dispatch-edge edits.
Use edit-scoped transactions with dependency completeness checks and whole-program fallback when alias or dispatch provenance is incomplete.
Which dependency-completeness invariant detects missing alias or dispatch justifications before committing an incremental finding set?
For each affected producer, independently enumerated summary, heap, and dispatch consumers must match version-current reverse dependencies.
Inject dropped heap and dispatch reverse links into SCCUpdate v3; independently enumerate consumers and verify transaction rejection before findings commit.
Three injected dispatch-link losses in newly activated contexts escaped both enumerators, allowing stale findings to commit.
Forward-scan affected and newly reachable contexts for dispatch targets and heap uses, comparing derived dependencies with reverse indexes before commit.
After three escaped dispatch-link losses, add source-level forward scans for activated contexts and fall back when derived dependencies disagree.
Implement forward dependency scans in SCCUpdate v3; inject lost links and measure fallback correctness and DispatchDelta-100 speedup.
SCCUpdate v4 adds source-level dependency scans and transactional whole-program fallback when scanned heap or dispatch consumers disagree with reverse indexes.
SCCUpdate v4 detected all three injected link losses, fell back to matching findings, and achieved 3.0× median speedup on DispatchDelta-100.
Adopt SCCUpdate v4, retaining alias-kill revocation and conditional SCC rebuilding; fallback detected injected faults while maintaining 3.0× median speedup.
